name: Soil Moisture
description: Path 2 (grass path) is likely significantly affected by soil moisture. Wet soil creates much higher rolling resistance. The bimodality likely represents 'dry' and 'wet' clusters of travel times. Path 1 is less affected. This is the most probable explanation given the context.

name: Rainfall
description: Directly related to soil moisture. Recent rainfall would create the 'wet' conditions affecting Path 2's travel time. It would show as a distinct travel time cluster.  Path 1 being a track would be less affected.

name: Crop Row Condition (Path 2)
description: Variations in the condition of the crop rows themselves along Path 2. Uneven rows, debris, or differing crop heights will create drag and slow the robot, resulting in multiple time clusters. Different sections of the field may have varying row conditions.

name: Time of Day / Dew Formation
description: Dew or frost on the grass of Path 2 can significantly slow travel time, creating a distinct cluster of slower times. This is time-dependent and affects Path 2 much more than the track.

name: Path 2 Traffic (Human/Animal)
description: If people or animals frequently use Path 2, they can compact or damage sections, leading to differing travel times. Tracks would be less susceptible to this.

name: Battery Level
description: Lower battery levels can cause the robot to reduce motor power to conserve energy, affecting travel speed.  The bimodality could represent 'fully charged' versus 'low battery' states. This would affect both paths but *could* manifest more clearly on the more energy intensive Path 2.

name: Robot Payload
description: If the robot carries varying payloads (e.g., different sensor packages or collected samples), this will affect its speed.  This is an operational factor. The bimodality could be 'empty' versus 'full'.

name: Temperature
description: Temperature impacts battery performance (lower temperatures reduce capacity).  Also, extreme temperatures could affect motor performance. Less direct than soil moisture, but still a factor. This could subtly shift travel times across both paths.

name: Sun Angle / Shadowing
description: Shadows cast by crops or other field features could affect the robot's camera-based navigation, potentially causing it to slow down or take slightly different routes, leading to time variations. More prominent on Path 2 as it’s between rows.

name: Wind Speed/Direction
description: Strong winds can create resistance, especially on Path 2. Wind direction would matter; headwind = slower, tailwind = faster. Less impact on the more sheltered Path 1.

name: Wheel Slip (Path 2)
description: The grass surface of Path 2 is more prone to wheel slip, especially when wet. This would reduce effective speed and add variation.  The amount of slip could create distinct clusters.

name: Plant Growth Stage
description: As crops grow, the density and height of the plants along Path 2 will increase, causing more resistance and slowing travel time.  Different stages of growth would create clusters.

name: Track Condition (Path 1)
description: While generally more stable, Path 1 could have variations – potholes, loose gravel, or uneven sections. These would be less frequent than Path 2 issues, but could still cause some travel time variations.

name: Robot Software Version
description: Updates to the navigation software or motor control algorithms could inadvertently affect travel time. Changes in how the robot handles variations in terrain or power management could contribute to the observed bimodality.

name: Time of Year
description: Seasonality affects several other factors (plant growth, soil moisture). While not a direct cause, it impacts the distribution of times for other parameters.
